#!/bin/bash

# Flux batch script converted from Slurm
# Note: Flux does not support in-script directives for resource specification
# This script should be submitted with the following command:
# flux batch -N 1 -n 1 -c 4 -g 1 -t 10m --job-name=job_wgpu --output=./{id}_{name}.out --error=./{id}_{name}.err script.sh
#
# Resource specifications:
# -N 1         : 1 node (implicit from single task)
# -n 1         : 1 task (implicit from original, no --ntasks specified)
# -c 4         : 4 cores per task (from -c 4)
# -g 1         : 1 GPU (from --gres=gpu:1)
# -t 10m       : 10 minute walltime (from --time=00:10:00)
# --job-name=job_wgpu : job name (from --job-name=job_wgpu)
# --output=./{id}_{name}.out : output file with job ID and name
# --error=./{id}_{name}.err : error file with job ID and name
#
# Note: Flux uses {id} for job ID and {name} for job name
# Slurm uses %j for job ID and %x for job name

# Original Slurm job name: job_wgpu
# Flux: --job-name=job_wgpu

# Original Slurm output/error files: ./%j_%x.out and ./%j_%x.err
# Flux equivalent: ./{id}_{name}.out and ./{id}_{name}.err
# Note: Flux placeholder syntax differs from Slurm

# Original Slurm --open-mode=append
# Note: Flux does not have a direct equivalent for --open-mode=append
# Performance impact: Output files will be truncated (overwritten) rather than appended
# If append behavior is critical, use shell redirection (>>) in the script
# or manage output files manually

# Original Slurm --export=ALL
# Note: Flux batch jobs inherit the environment from submission shell by default
# Performance impact: Environment inheritance behavior is similar
# If specific environment control is needed, use --env or --env-remove at submission

# Original Slurm --time=00:10:00 (10 minutes)
# Flux: -t 10m or -t 600s

# Original Slurm --gres=gpu:1 (1 GPU)
# Flux: -g 1
# Note: GPU type cannot be specified in standard Flux syntax
# Performance impact: Job may be allocated any available GPU type

# Original Slurm --mem=64G (64 GB memory)
# Note: Flux memory specification uses --setattr or similar mechanisms
# Memory can be specified at submission:
# flux batch --setattr=system.memory=64G ...
# Or: --setattr=system.memory=65536M (64 * 1024 MB)
# Performance impact: Without explicit memory specification, job gets default allocation
# which may be insufficient for memory-intensive tasks
# Consult Flux documentation for memory allocation syntax at your site

# Original Slurm -c 4 (4 CPUs per task)
# Flux: -c 4

singularity exec --nv --overlay $SCRATCH/overlay-50G-10M.ext3:ro /scratch/work/public/singularity/cuda10.1-cudnn7-devel-ubuntu18.04-20201207.sif /bin/bash -c "

source /ext3/env.sh
conda activate

python ./test_gpu.py
"

# Complete submission command with all options:
# flux batch -N 1 -n 1 -c 4 -g 1 -t 10m \
#   --job-name=job_wgpu \
#   --output=./{id}_{name}.out \
#   --error=./{id}_{name}.err \
#   --setattr=system.memory=64G \
#   script.sh
#
# Note: Adjust memory attribute syntax based on your Flux installation
# Alternative memory syntax: --setattr=system.memory=65536M

issues: The script correctly documents resource specifications and properly converts Slurm directives to Flux command-line options.

Memory specification is documented but NOT included in the primary submission command at the top. The primary command should include '--setattr=system.memory=64G' to match the original Slurm --mem=64G requirement.

The output/error file placeholders use '{id}' and '{name}' syntax. Flux typically uses '{{id}}' (double braces) or '{{jobid}}' for job IDs. The single brace syntax should be verified against the specific Flux version being used.

The memory attribute syntax '--setattr=system.memory=64G' may not be correct for all Flux versions. The attribute path 'system.memory' should be verified. Common alternatives include '--setattr=memory=64G' or other site-specific attribute paths.

The complete submission command at the bottom of the script includes memory specification, but the primary command at the top does not. This inconsistency should be resolved by including memory in the primary command.
The script correctly notes that Flux does not support --open-mode=append, but does not provide a workaround. If append behavior is needed, the script should implement it using shell redirection.
No validation that the singularity container and overlay files exist before attempting to execute.
The $SCRATCH environment variable is used without validation that it is set.
GPU type specificity is lost in conversion (original may have been gpu:type:1 in Slurm, Flux only supports -g 1 for count).
